scene: A helmeted stunt rider stands up on the pegs of his motorbike at the lip of a wide desert canyon and punches one arm high overhead with the thumb up, twisting back over his shoulder. Red rock, kicked dust, hard midday sun.

A man in black tactical armour bows deeply from the waist, both palms pressed flat together and lifted to his forehead, head lowered, rifle slung behind him. A splintered doorway stands open at his back. Dim hallway, dust hanging in a shaft of light.

A man in a raincoat spins round in a café doorway with both arms flung up and his shoulders hunched to his ears, face screwed up. Slices of toast hang in the air above him and a tray lies upended at his feet. Warm café light.

A boy at a breakfast table hoists an enormous jar upside down over one tall glass with both hands, orange powder pouring out in a thick stream and clouding the air around him. Cereal bowls sit forgotten beside him. Morning light through thin curtains.

A man stands dead still in a packed night market with one arm stretched straight up above the heads around him and a phone pressed to his other ear. The crowd streams past him in a blur. String lights, food steam, warm night.

A shopper strides away down a covered market aisle with a folded shirt tucked under one arm, holding a single small coin up in his raised free hand and grinning back over his shoulder. Hanging garments, strip lights, a crowded aisle behind him.

A woman stops dead in her own kitchen doorway with both hands still gripping the frame, chin lifted and eyes wide at a brown hen strutting across the breakfast table between the plates and the teapot. Morning light stripes the floor tiles.

A grinning chef swings a heavy cleaver down onto a board heaped with spring onions, caught mid-strike with her whole shoulder behind it. Chopped piles fan across the steel counter and a vast crate of vegetables waits beside her. Steam, hard kitchen light.

An old fortune teller lunges across a spread of cards and throws one arm straight out at the viewer, finger extended, rings on every finger, eyes wide and certain. Heavy red cloth drapes the booth behind her. Candlelight, deep shadow.

A man kneels and presses his ear flat against the lid of a heavy wooden coffin, both palms braced on the wood, eyes wide and body rigid. A single candle lights the stone crypt around him. Damp walls, cobwebs, one small flame.

A hen stands on a burst sack of grain with her beak wide open mid-squawk, both wings half spread and her neck thrown forward. Other hens come running across the farmyard behind her. Spilled feed, trampled straw, hard morning light.

A young woman grips a friend by the sleeve and hauls him with her whole body toward a glowing karaoke doorway, laughing, leaning into the pull. He stumbles along after her. Wet pavement, reflected neon, scooters parked along the kerb.

A woman holds a single small coin up at the end of an outstretched arm in front of an open freezer, the coin furred white with frost, cold vapour spilling down past her hand. Dim kitchen, pale blue light from the freezer.

A boy raises a nearly empty paper bag high overhead and shakes it upside down over his open palm, where one small red chilli has landed. Kitchen shelves and a steaming pot stand behind him. Warm afternoon light through a window.

A man stands well back from an enormous splattered canvas on a white gallery wall, his head tilted hard to one side and his weight slumped onto one hip, arms folded. Spotlights, polished concrete floor, bare walls stretching away.

A small boy grips the stern rail of a wooden ferry and leans far out over the churning white wake, mouth open in a shout, hair flattened by the wind. Passengers sit in the shade behind him. Hard glare off the water.

A boy on a doorstep holds a brown-paper parcel tied with string out at full arm's length, pushing it forward with both hands. A man's hands reach in from the edge of the frame to take it. Terrace houses, milk bottles, flat morning light.

A woman crouches low at an open fuse box on a darkened market stall and reaches deep inside it with a hairpin, her whole body leaning into the gap. The stalls either side blaze with light. Tangled cables, stacked crates, night.

A toddler stands gripping the arm of a chair in a living room with her mouth open mid-sound, chin lifted and one hand thrown out. An adult behind her has frozen mid-movement, a teacup halfway to her lips. Warm afternoon light.

A man rises onto his tiptoes at the tail of an enormous queue, stretching his whole body upward and craning to see the distant front, a bag abandoned at his feet. The line snakes twice around a concrete building. Hot sun, hundreds of shoulders.

A big weathered man throws his arm across a dinner table and claps his open palm flat over the mouth of his glass. A tilted bottle stops short just above his hand. Plates pushed back, crumpled cloth, warm evening light.

A woman recoils from a jeweller's counter with both arms flung up and her weight thrown backward, staring at a tall tottering stack of gold coins beside one tiny gold ring on a velvet pad. Bright spotlights, glass cases, dark wood.

A doctor in a white coat leans forward and holds a brimming spoon of dark syrup out at arm's length, a bottle tipped and already pouring in her other hand, stethoscope swinging loose. A clinic couch and a glass cabinet stand behind her.

A soaked man at the stern of an overloaded wooden lifeboat heaves a suitcase over the side with one arm while the other clamps a dented tin can hard against his chest. Grey swell, low sky, hunched passengers along the gunwales.

A woman turns her whole body in a plain sitting room and thrusts one rigid arm out toward the corner where two walls meet. A small boy already stands in that corner with his back to her, head down. Afternoon light through net curtains.

A man sitting on a clinic couch with both trouser legs rolled up swings his open palm down hard onto his own bare knee, arm caught mid-strike, jaw set. Paper-covered couch, a glass cabinet, flat overhead light.

A Thai dancer in a gold headdress and long silk skirt turns mid-movement on a dark stage, her skirt sweeping a wide circle and one arm curving high overhead. One half of her is lit warm gold, the other lost in shadow.

A small boy tips his head right back at a street chai stall with his mouth hanging open, staring up at a long ribbon of milky tea falling from a high pot into a low one. His own cup dangles forgotten at his side. Dusk, steam, warm lamps.

A man throws his head back laughing and swings one arm wide in dismissal, the front of his shirt soaked dark and dripping. A tipped tumbler dangles from a hand at the edge of the frame. Crowded wooden bar, bottles, warm low light.

A man in a bowler hat and a long dark coat stands rigid under a black umbrella in sheeting rain, glaring down at a cup and saucer balanced on a low wall, his face red with fury. Grey street, running gutters, flat light.

A child flings a spadeful of dark crumbly soil back over one shoulder in a churned vegetable patch, mouth open in a shriek, earth hanging in the air around her. Spades and upturned clods litter the crater. A garden fence, grey daylight.

A woman grips a steering wheel with both hands and leans hard to her right, head turned down the right-hand branch of a rural fork, brow furrowed. The front wheels have begun to swing that way. Lone tree, dust, flat afternoon light.

A teacher stands in a dusty school courtyard at morning assembly with one arm raised straight overhead. Rows of children in white shirts and navy shorts stand motionless in front of her, facing a long low building with an open verandah. Bright early light.

A mobile phone lies face down in a shallow puddle on an empty tarmac road, seen low and close, rain bouncing off its back in bright crowns. The street beyond dissolves into grey water and blurred headlights. Cold flat daylight.

A woman kneels barefoot on a pavement at dawn and spoons rice into a monk's alms bowl, both arms extended and her head bowed low. The monk stands motionless above her in saffron robes. Mist, gold low light, shuttered shopfronts.

A small girl stretches up on tiptoe on a wooden stool, one arm reaching at full extension toward a plain jar on the highest kitchen shelf, fingers well short of it. Shelves of tins and crockery around her. Plain morning light.
